request.system:
You are assisting with the qualitative analysis of interview data from a study of frontline hotel employees' work experiences. You will receive one passage from an interview transcript. Code the passage as a qualitative researcher would in first-order coding, and complete the coding form below.

About the passage
- The passage begins with brief details about the interviewee: role, gender and years in the job.
- Lines marked "Interviewer:" are the interviewer's questions. Lines marked "Interviewee:" are the interviewee's answers.
- Some passages contain two excerpts from the same interview, marked [Earlier in the interview] and [Later in the interview].

The coding form
1. codes: Give between 3 and 6 first-order codes. Each code has a short label of 2 to 6 words, kept close to the interviewee's own language, and one supporting quote. Each quote must be copied word for word from the passage, without any change, and must be no longer than 30 words.
2. interpretation: In one or two sentences, in your own words, state what the interviewee is communicating in this passage.
3. tone: The overall tone of the interviewee's account. Choose one: positive, negative, mixed or neutral.
4. confidence: An integer from 0 to 100 indicating how confident you are that your interpretation is accurate.

Respond only with a JSON object that follows the schema provided. Write in English.
request.user:
Interviewee details: Front-office cashier, male, 6th year

Interviewer: I hear your former front-office manager left this year. What was the reason?

Interviewee: Regarding this matter, the hotel has an official position: the employment relationship was terminated by amicable mutual agreement on the basis of personal career planning. That’s what the email said too, and all staff received it. In the month before she left, Finance came to audit the accounts several times, mainly the signatures on some discount slips and complimentary-room slips. What exactly they were checking, we on the cashier side don’t really know. We’re only responsible for submitting the slips according to procedure. The signature box isn’t our concern. During that period her office door was always closed. Twice people from Finance went in and stayed the whole afternoon. Some of the slips were... were instructions passed down from above, and we didn’t... (pauses) Anyway, we on the front line aren’t involved in any of that. Leaving was her personal decision. Reportedly, when she left, all the formalities went very smoothly and the handover was very complete, so nobody asked much. On her last day at work, she left at three in the afternoon. She didn’t have a meal with everyone. Her husband came by car to collect her things. She was a really nice person. Whenever a guest complained, she’d come out and stand between us and them, and at New Year she’d give each of us a red envelope, out of her own pocket. Oh, by the way, the new manager started last month, and our front-office cashier system has been upgraded too. Now guests can pay by scanning a code, invoices are much quicker, and the queues at peak check-out time are half as long. It used to be that at twelve noon the queue in the lobby would stretch right to the door. Would you like to have a look? I can give you a demonstration. From swiping the key card to printing the invoice, it only takes a minute. The system was procured centrally by the group, and every hotel uses it now.

He mentions the official reason for the manager's departure: mutual agreement based on personal career planning. That's one code. Then, there's the audit by Finance, checking discount and complimentary slips. The cashier's role is just submitting them, not knowing the details. That's another code about Finance audit and lack of knowledge. 

He also talks about the manager's office being closed, Finance people staying the whole afternoon. That could be a code about manager's isolation or secrecy. Then, the smooth handover and the manager being nice, giving red envelopes. That's positive traits of the manager. 

The new manager and system upgrade are also mentioned, so a code about system upgrade and efficiency improvements. The part about the new system reducing queue times is another point.

Now, the interpretation. The interviewee is explaining the manager's departure as per the hotel's official statement, but also hints at possible scrutiny from Finance. He acknowledges the manager's positive qualities but also notes the changes and improvements with the new system.

Tone seems mixed. There's some negative aspects (audit, possible issues) but also positive (manager's kindness, new system benefits). So mixed tone.

Confidence in interpretation: High, since the codes cover both the official explanation, the audit, the manager's traits, and the new system. The quotes are directly taken from the text. The interpretation captures both the official reasons and the underlying context.
